subject: AWS/GCP/Azure Marketplace private offer - unit price mapping and next steps
messages:
From: Janelle Sykes <janelle.sykes@brightcart.com>

Cc: ams-marketplace@amazon.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer discussion - token volumes

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier - that was helpful. Per our call, here's the initial volume profile for BrightCart's LLM usage:

- Expected active users: 1.2M monthly
- Avg prompt length: ~280 tokens in, ~320 tokens out (combined ~600 tokens per request)
- Peak concurrent requests estimate: ~350 RPS for Black Friday-like events
- Estimated monthly tokens: ~720M - 1.1B tokens (varies with features rolled out)

We discussed wanting to target a 1M-token unit price (list) that maps cleanly to AWS Marketplace private offer terms. Budget range for FY27 procurement is $180k - $300k/month for inference (they're evaluating tradeoffs across quantization and batch constraints).

Attached: brightcart_expected_tokens.csv (samples + monthly projection).

Can you confirm what unit $/1M tokens map to on AWS private offers vs. Redwood hosted invoice? Also the timing and docs you need from our procurement team to start a private offer flow.

Thanks,
Janelle
Head of AI Product, BrightCart
[Attachment: brightcart_expected_tokens.csv (csv)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer discussion - token volumes

Janelle - thanks for the detailed profile and the CSV, that helps a lot. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Recap:
- BrightCart expected tokens: ~0.72B-1.1B/month (we'll price for the higher bound for procurement purposes)
- Target budget: $180k-300k/mo inference spend

What we'll do next:
1) I'll loop in Aditya (pricing) to map target unit $/1M tokens to the AWS/GCP/Azure private offer construct and produce a unit-price mapping sheet for each marketplace (list price vs private-offer unit).
2) Laura will outline the procurement artifacts needed (SOW, invoice remit, tax forms, AWS private offer contact flow).
3) We'll include an example unit-price estimate at 0.9B tokens/mo and two scenarios (50% quantized, 8-bit local caching) so BrightCart can see tradeoffs.

Aditya - can you take the token profile and produce a simple mapping: list $/1M tokens (hosted), Redwood marketplace list price equivalent, and proposed private-offer unit price for AWS, GCP, and Azure? If you can include assumptions (e.g., expected cache hit, batching effect) and a target effective $/1M tokens that fits BrightCart's stated budget range, that'd be perfect.

Janelle - we'll aim to get a preliminary mapping and docs back by Monday (23 Nov). If procurement needs a faster turnaround for an internal approval cycle, tell me the deadline and we'll prioritize.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Janelle Sykes <janelle.sykes@brightcart.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ams-marketplace@amazon.com, marketplace-sales@gcp.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer discussion - unit price mapping (draft)

Marissa / Janelle - attaching a draft unit-price mapping and a short assumptions sheet. High level conclusions (see attached workbook for per-marketplace tabs):

- Assumptions used: 0.9B tokens/mo baseline; cache hit 12% (prefix caching + session reuse); batching gains ~8% effective token reduction for steady-state; 8-bit quantization savings scenario reduces compute by ~25% on average workloads.

- Redwood hosted list price (baseline): $25 / 1M tokens
- Marketplace list equivalence (unmodified): AWS/GCP/Azure marketplace list usually adds a marketplace fee - effective list mapping used: $27-30 / 1M tokens depending on marketplace fees and payment routing.

- Proposed private-offer unit prices to fit BrightCart budget ($180k-300k/mo):
  * Conservative (no quantization, minimal batching): $22 / 1M tokens -> 0.9B tokens -> $19.8k per 100M -> $198k/mo (fits lower-mid of range)
  * Recommended (expected caching + batching): $18 / 1M tokens -> 0.9B tokens -> $162k/mo (fits lower bound)
  * Aggressive (50% quantization on non-latency critical workloads): $12 / 1M tokens -> 0.9B tokens -> $108k/mo (well under budget, gives headroom)

Notes on marketplace: AWS private offers can accept a unit-price mapping as an API SKU line item. We recommend Redwood submit three SKUs (conservative/recommended/aggressive) and BrightCart choose which to sign up against; marketplace margins and payment routing can add 5-10% to the unit price compared to Redwood invoice. See tab "marketplace_notes" in the attached workbook for the exact markup examples. 

Attachments: redwood_marketplace_price_map.xlsx (tabs: assumptions, aws_private_offer_instructions, gcp_mapping, azure_mapping).

Next steps: Marissa/Laura - can you confirm these are the right three scenarios and that BrightCart wants the SKU lines prepared for an AWS private offer? Janelle - if you want us to push the recommended scenario into an internal procurement request at BrightCart, tell us which scenario to price into the purchase order.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Director, Pricing & GTM Economics, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_marketplace_price_map.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
